guide.intro: FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) is a lossless format that keeps every bit of the original recording while being 40–60% smaller than WAV. You usually meet it in CD rips, Bandcamp and Qobuz purchases, studio masters and hi-res downloads. A 4-minute FLAC song is typically 25–40 MB; the same song as a 192 kbps MP3 is about 6 MB. When a device, app or upload form wants MP3 instead, {brand} converts it right in your browser – fast, private and with the options normally hidden behind paid plans.
uses: Make FLAC files playable on a car stereo, older phone or smart TV.
Send FLAC recordings to people who need a universal format.
Prepare FLAC audio for an editor, transcription service or podcast host that wants MP3.
Batch-convert a folder of FLAC downloads in one go.
tips: Choose 192 kbps for music, 128 kbps for podcasts and 64–96 kbps mono for speech.
Mono halves the size of voice recordings with no loss in clarity.
22 kHz sample rate is plenty for speech and shrinks files further.
Use Audio Cutter afterwards to trim silence or make a ringtone.
Rename files before converting – the output keeps the original name.
more: FLAC vs MP3
